chunks: I believe in your Lord, so listen to me.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'I believe in your Lord, so listen to me' in Surah Yaseen?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often associated with the believer from the family of Pharaoh or the faithful man of the city of Yaseen, highlighting the courage of individual testimony against a tyrannous majority. It underscores the principle of *Tawhid* not merely as belief but as a public declaration that demands the attention of the community, serving as a model for early Shia figures who maintained faith amidst persecution. The phrase 'so listen to me' implies an expectation of acceptance, reflecting the authority of the true believer's word in the face of doubt.
